deliverables.text: A total-demand table: add up the capacity requests of all four active bids (Aurora Ridge, Cobalt Peak, Fenwick Yards, and Briar Hollow) from Appendix B, showing the running sum in block form at each step and the final total as a mixed number -- this tells Renata how much capacity the whole queue is asking for against a substation that cannot supply all of it.

The remaining-capacity calculation: starting from Appendix A's total substation capacity and already-committed capacity, subtract to find the capacity actually remaining for today's decision, then subtract Aurora Ridge's request from that remaining capacity to find exactly how much would be left over (or stranded) under Option A -- every step shown in fraction/mixed-number form using a common denominator, including any regrouping the subtraction requires.

The combined-bid calculation: add Cobalt Peak's and Fenwick Yards's capacity requests together to find their combined size, and show explicitly whether that combined size fits inside the remaining capacity found in D2 -- the addition must use a common denominator across the two bids' unlike denominators.

The head-to-head comparison: subtract the combined Cobalt Peak + Fenwick Yards request (D3) from the remaining capacity (D2) to find exactly how much would be left over under Option B, then state which option -- A or B -- leaves less capacity stranded, with the difference shown as a fraction of a block.

An original visual display (a scaled capacity-bar diagram, in the substation's block units) showing, side by side, how much of the remaining capacity is used and how much is stranded under Option A versus under Option B, built directly from your D2 and D4 figures.

appendices.title: Fenwick Creek Substation: Capacity of Record

balance.argument_a: Aurora Ridge is engineering-cleared and ready to sign today, with no dependency on any other bid confirming; its request (2-7/8 blocks) nearly fills the 3-3/8 blocks remaining, leaving only 1/2 block (12 MW) stranded. See FACILITATOR.md for the full arithmetic.
balance.argument_b: Cobalt Peak and Fenwick Yards, added together (2-11/12 blocks), fit inside the same remaining capacity and leave only 11/24 block (11 MW) stranded -- genuinely less than Option A -- but require both bids to confirm before the queue deadline, a real risk Option A does not carry. See FACILITATOR.md for the full arithmetic.
balance.margin_basis: margin = |stranded_A - stranded_B| / max(stranded_A, stranded_B), where stranded_A = remaining_capacity - Aurora_Ridge_request and stranded_B = remaining_capacity - (Cobalt_Peak_request + Fenwick_Yards_request), all in block units, computed entirely in fraction/mixed-number arithmetic. remaining_capacity = total_capacity - already_committed (Appendix A). Using this case's own fixed Appendix A/B block figures: total=4-5/8, committed=1-1/4, remaining=3-3/8; Aurora Ridge=2-7/8 so stranded_A=1/2; Cobalt Peak + Fenwick Yards=1-1/4+1-2/3=2-11/12 so stranded_B=11/24. margin = |1/2 - 11/24| / (1/2) = (12/24-11/24)/(12/24) = (1/24)/(12/24) = 1/12 = 8.33%. Option B (the combined smaller bids) leaves less stranded capacity and wins under this case's own fixed numbers -- this arithmetic does not depend on Appendix C/D's block-size figure at all, since it cancels out of a same-units fraction comparison; the block-size MW figure only converts the answer into a real-world megawatt quantity for the pitch's narrative framing, it never changes which option wins in block terms.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Size, in megawatts, of one Fenwick Creek capacity allocation block
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source states a capacity-block size for this exact fictional substation. RMI's large-load interconnection guidance [S5] reports that loads exceeding approximately 20 MW require direct transmission-level connection -- a real, published order-of-magnitude reference point for how utilities size a 'large load' study increment. 24 MW is chosen near that real reference point, scaled up slightly so the substation's stated total (4-5/8 blocks) and committed (1-1/4 blocks) capacities land on whole-megawatt figures for the pitch's narrative.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The block size does not change which option wins -- Option A vs. Option B is decided by a same-units fraction comparison in blocks (case.json.balance.margin_basis), and the block's MW size cancels out of that comparison entirely. It only rescales the real-world megawatt figures the pitch reports. A Hero who argues the real increment should be smaller or larger should recompute the MW figures, not the block-fraction comparison -- Tier 2 P5 will confirm this parameter does not flip the verdict under a +/-50% flex.

sensitivity_note: No illness, death, or severe hardship; ordinary workplace time-pressure (a same-day decision deadline). SPEC SS6 one-line flag not required beyond noting the deadline stress for the discussion lead.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: No public source states Fenwick Creek's own capacity-block MW size -- 24 MW (MA1) is a constructed, disclosed Modeling Assumption grounded near RMI's real ~20 MW large-load transmission-interconnection threshold [S5], not a measurable present fact about a specific real substation. Unlike a typical load-bearing scenario dial, this parameter is expected NOT to flip the verdict, since the A-vs-B comparison is a same-units fraction comparison in blocks that the MW scale cancels out of; Tier 2 P5 will confirm this mechanically.
